Republic of the Phili rue DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AN X'O_ ELEAS D EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal Quezon City DATE; LEGAL SERV CE DILG Legal Opinion No. 01 s. 2012 [JAN 4 2012 ATTY. DANILO O. LEYBLE City Mayor CITY OF ANTIPOLO Dear Mayor Danilo O. Leyble: This is in response to your letter re vesting that this Department AFFIRM the validity of City Ordinance NO. 2010-422 0 Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLOP) and City Zoning Ordinance enacted on 06 December 2010. The subject ordinance was passed in view of the expiration of the prior CLUP/Zoning Ordinance for the period 2000-2010. In your letter you mentioned that the subject ordinance wa endorsed by the Office of the City Mayor to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for purpose of review on 10 January 2011, and a Revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan (2010-2020) was submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on 08 September 2011, integrating therein the comments and recommendations made by the members of the Provincial Land Use Committee as transmitted by Ms. En.P. Gertie A. Sisdfi, Provincial Planning and Development Coordinator (PPDC). In between, there were conflicting views held by Ms. Sison and your City Planning and Development Coordinator (CPDC) Mr. Renato Matienzo. According to your letter, Ms. Sison remained steadfast in her position that the subject ordinance is invalid for non- compliance to the procedural policies mandated by the HLURB Board Resolution No. 789, series of 2006 and that the new site of the public market where construction is on- going is not allowed under the prior/old CLUP and City Ordinance for 2000-2010. Thus, Ms. Sison held that the subject ordinance is ineffective and inoperative until approved by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal. On the other hand, Mr. Matienzo (CPD) subscribed to the view that the subject ordinance is a valid enactment of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo, and the site of the new public market had been classified as a major commercial zone under the said new city zoning ordinance. In his letter to Ms. Sison dated 17 November 2011, Mr. Matienzo cited DILG Opinion No. 121-1993 which in sum holds that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's power to REVIEW consist of examination of the ordinance within the prescribed period of thirty (30) days and if no action is taken, the ordinance is presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. It may also declare the same invalid on the SOLE ground that such ordinance is BEYOND THE POWER conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod. Therefore, in addressing your request, please be informed that the Department is without mandate to affirm the validity of any ordinance for that matter. We note that Mr. Matienzo cited DILG Opinion No. 121-1993 which this Department finds still applicable in resolving the issues at hand, citing Sections 56 and 455 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1990. In addition thereto, we cite the case of Moday vs Court of Appeals, G.R. No. 107916, 20 February 1997 wherein the Supreme Court held that the upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance, or order is 'beyond the powers conferred upon the council or president making the same. ' Absolutely no other ground is recognized by

the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance, or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance, or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council Or president. " (emphasis and underscoring supplied) Finally, for your further guidance and reference, we have attached the following DILG Opinion Nos. 122-2003, 17-2004, 60-2008 and 43-2009. Very truly yours, ESU Direct LS:55 QUE Ill Sign ure ame te
